'''Davis:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} | title = [[Governor of Kansas|Governor]] | before_election = [[Sam Brownback]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Sam Brownback]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | image2_size = 150x150px }} {{ElectionsKS}} The '''2014 Kansas gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[List of governors of Kansas|governor of Kansas]]. It was held concurrently with the [[2014 United States Senate election in Kansas|election]] of Kansas' [[Classes of United States senators|Class II U.S. Senate seat]], elections to the [[2014 United States Senate elections|United States Senate]] in other states, elections to the [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|United States House of Representatives]], and various state and local elections. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Sam Brownback]] ran for re-election to a second term. He was opposed in the general election by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Paul Davis (Kansas politician)|Paul Davis]], the minority leader of the [[Kansas House of Representatives]], and Libertarian attorney Keen Umbehr. The election was viewed as a referendum on Brownback's [[Kansas experiment|aggressive tax cutting initiatives]] and his conservative values.{{cite web|url=http://kansasfirstnews.com/2014/11/04/brownback-defeats-davis-in-kansas-governors-race|title=Brownback defeats Davis in Kansas Governor's race|access-date=2014-11-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129151708/http://kansasfirstnews.com/2014/11/04/brownback-defeats-davis-in-kansas-governors-race/|archive-date=2014-11-29|url-status=dead}} The consensus among ''[[The Cook Political Report]]'', ''[[Governing (magazine)|Governing]]'', ''[[Stuart Rothenberg|The Rothenberg Political Report]]'', ''[[Sabato's Crystal Ball]]'', ''Daily Kos Elections'', and others was that the contest was a tossup. Brownback won the election by a margin of 3.69%. Davis carried seven counties, all in eastern Kansas.
